newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

* The Federal Trade Commission rejected Staples Inc's proposed acquisition of Office Depot Inc and voted to seek a Federal court ruling to block the merger on grounds that it would raise prices on office supplies.

* Newmont Mining won its effort to acquire Santa Fe Pacific Gold for $2.43 billion in stock, and analysts are expecting more consolidations, possibly involving Battle Mountain Gold Co, Getchell Gold Corp or Barrick Gold.

* The near collapse of giant Canadian retailer T. Eaton Co has heightened fears that even Canada's most powerful companies are being threatened by aggressive American rivals such as Wal-Mart and Home Depot.
* Procter & Gamble, which owns three daytime television dramas, is seeking to reverse falling audience ratings for television soap operas as it spends more dollars advertising during such programs.
* Niagara Mohawk Power agreed to a $4 billion buyout of long-term contracts with most of its independent power producers.
* The Dow industrials soared 78.50 points to close at a record 7,079.39.
* The yield on the 30-year Treasury was unchanged at 6.81 percent.

* Nationwide Insurance agreed to invest $13 million in minority communities to settle a Justice Department suit accusing the nation's fifth largest insurer of discrimination in inner city neighborhoods.
* General Electric agreed to buy Greenwich Air Services and UNC Inc for $875 million in cash and stock.
* The Japanese Government said it would introduce digital television before 2000, speeding up its original plans by several years.

* General Motors said it would put all North American car manufacturing under the direction of Donald Hackworth and have the executive who built its Saturn division develop companywide management and engineering practices.
* Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley have agreed to keep Morgan Stanley's general counsel, Jonathan Clark, thereby resolving one issue in their pending merger.
* Merrill Lynch Chairman Daniel Tully received about a 40 percent pay raise last year, when his compensation rose to more than $10 million.

* At least six Japanese asset management companies have suspended business with Nomura Securities in the wake of the company's announcement that two of its directors had made unauthorized stock trades.
* The Thai Cabinet is scheduled to vote today on a Government plan to end the country's financial turmoil by creating a company to lend $3.86 billion to property developers.
* To encourage a trade pact with the United States, the Vietnamese government has agreed to repay millions of dollars in debts incurred by the former South Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
